Priya / team —

Quick read on the numbers. Using Acme's 120 concurrent chat estimate and median message length ~250 tokens, the two scenario outputs are attached (I exported slices into the PDF for quick review). Short version:

- Conservative (40 reserved slots): serves sustained baseline of ~55 concurrent sessions with good p95 latency (<90ms token time) and uses burst credits to handle spikes. 40 reserved slots assumes autoscaling headroom and prefix caching; peak with burst looks OK for a brief window but prolonged weeks-long demand will deplete crediting.

- Aggressive (70 reserved slots): comfortably covers sustained 120 concurrent sessions with low p95 (<=60ms) and minimal queueing, but roughly doubles monthly committed cost. Also increases our risk exposure if Acme doesn't convert after pilot.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Lead time for adding dedicated slots (reserved) is ~2–3 weeks for procurement + infra provisioning; earlier sign is better.
- If we go shared-burst only, we can start faster (3–4 days) but we need a burst credit allocation of ~250k tokens/day to simulate sustained peak for pilot — cost is unpredictable and we can't guarantee p95 at the aggressive level.
- I'll add a simple pump-failover plan: prefer reserved for predictable SLA in pilot, fallback to burst with traffic shaping if provisioning slips.

I'll bring the detailed numbers to tomorrow's sync and drop the scenario exports into the Drive link.

—Marcus

Subject: Re: Pilot timing & fleet needs (Acme) — cost and contractual notes

Team —

Thanks Marcus — that aligns with what I expected. Quick finance notes for the two scenarios:

- Reserved 40 slots: incremental committed cost ~USD 42k/month; pilot discount (standard) reduces first-quarter invoice by 15%. This keeps pilot bookkeeping simple but means we carry the utilization risk if they don't convert.

- Reserved 70 slots: ~USD 72k/month committed; we can offer a stepped commitment (50 slots month 1, 70 month 2) to reduce initial exposure — would require explicit milestone language in SOW.

- Shared-burst option: low upfront, but if we need to allocate temporary burst credits for sustained peak, expected pilot spend could spike to ~USD 35–50k for that month depending on traffic. Procurement will push for a cap and defined burn window.

Action items for procurement: we need explicit conversion milestones and a short termination clause for pilot non-convert. If we plan to ramp to 70 slots in month 2, include a 14-day notice before ramp.

I'll prepare a redline-friendly SOW snippet for the stepped-commitment approach and upload to the Drive link.

—Laura
